pr_title: drivers: intc: plic: set edge-triggered register address using compat
pr_body:
Define the edge-trigger register base address based on whether the PLIC node in the devicetree has an additional compatible that supports edge-triggered interrupt.

Limited the implementation to Andes NCEPLIC100 only, updated the devicetree binding of `andes_v5_ae350` accordingly.

**Caveat**: Per-instance trigger register address isn't supported, if one of the PLIC instances has `"andestech,plic"`, it assumes that all PLIC instances have the same type

Fixes #64675
pr_comments: Pulling this back as draft as it has a commit from #65847, but feel free to review
@fkokosinski - any general thoughts about this PR?
can someone from Andes confirm that the nceplic100 is present on all types of cores supported by the upstream `andes_v5_ae350` platform please? cc @kevinwang821020 @jimmyzhe

Hi @ycsin, 

yes, currently `andes_v5_ae350` represents ae350 bitstream integrated with NCEPLIC100.
We also have some ae350 bitstreams integrated with standard CLIC instead of PLIC, but they do not yet support Zephyr upstream.

issue_context.title: [riscv-privileged] PLIC is not compliant with the Spec
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**

RISC-V PLIC driver no more conforms to the Spec after the 8db1a5a, see https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/63273

Trigger Type register is not defined in the recent PLIC Spec and so is not compliant with RISC-V Privileged Standard: https://github.com/riscv/riscv-plic-spec/blob/master/riscv-plic-1.0.0.pdf
IMHO this is a miss in the Spec and it results in a situation when all the vendors who support Triggering type configuration implement it in a proprietary way, using the custom offsets and custom codes for the triggering types.

So until the Trigger Type becomes a standard, it would be nice if we leave a room for flexibility here: by default PLIC should be compliant with the Spec while the Trigger Type register could be optionally enabled  as an extension for particular platforms. 

**Environment**
Zephyr v3.5

* Page: `project/issues`
* Version: main
* SHA-1: 8db1a5add221b5e47ad4e01dfcb3b4064a8299f4
comments: This is currently being escalated, see https://github.com/riscv/riscv-plic-spec/issues/52, are you using some PLIC that has a different offset for the trigger type registers?

Hi @ycsin , 

> This is currently being escalated, see [riscv/riscv-plic-spec#52](https://github.com/riscv/riscv-plic-spec/issues/52),

Thanks! Nice to know there is already a ticket for the RISC-V Spec.

>  are you using some PLIC that has a different offset for the trigger type registers?

Right, we have some similar register called IRQ triggering mode and it has different offset: 
https://github.com/syntacore/zephyr/blob/sc/main-3.4/soc/riscv/riscv-privileged/syntacore-scr/common/plic.c

We implemented it as a proprietary SoC-specific extension for a regular standard PLIC. 
It's not yet upstreamed but we are working in this direction

review_comments: Why do we have different policies to report the IRQ handling completion for EDGE-triggered and LEVEL-triggered modes? Why one is reported earlier while the other one later?

Yeah, acking works exactly the same for edge/level irqs, so we should unify this while we're at it. Could you do it @ycsin? Thanks!

The rest LGTM
If we really can combine it, then we don't need to introduce riscv_plic_irq_trig_val at all, right?
Yup, that's correct. But let's wait for @ycsin to confirm that :)

Hey all, I had a look and that seems to be a workaround for Andes' NCEPLIC100, see https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/dd46337ca69662b6912bc230d393c4261d126b8f and the discussion [here](https://lore.kernel.org/linux-arm-kernel/CA+V-a8s80shYtUsJZSu7vz_S6ZXtxGkHVi5cgBWO9tr_n+XiJA@mail.gmail.com/t/)

Hi @ycsin, 

Interesting! Looks like Andes's PLIC has an issue?

From the thread you've shared:
```
> Is this a feature of this PLIC implementation? Or is that common to
> all PLICs?
>
I think it's a feature of this PLIC implementation and not common to all PLIC's.
```

I think making this WAR behavior default for all the vendors is very risky.

Just as a follow-up. Syntacore also has this Triggering Mode register, but since it is not standardized yet, we made it as extension for standard PLIC: https://github.com/syntacore/zephyr/blob/sc/main-3.5/soc/riscv/riscv-privileged/syntacore-scr/common/plic.c

I suppose that other vendors also have some differences in that non-standard functionality implementation and bringing this to a common PLIC driver which is intended to follow the Spec is a "thin ice" path
